what: Brazil monitors two patients for possible Ebola infection

clean_source_blocks.text: Health authorities in Brazil are monitoring two patients for possible Ebola infection in the country's two biggest cities, São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro. A man, 37, from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo) "exhibited symptoms such as fever", São Paulo's state government said. In Rio state, the health department said it had activated safety protocols after a Belgian man who arrived from Uganda showed "viral symptoms such as cough, chills and diarrhoea". The test results for both patients should become available next week. If confirmed, they would be the first infection cases outside Africa since the outbreak began in DR Congo. There are now more than 1,000 suspected Ebola cases in DR Congo, with at least 246 deaths. Uganda has reported nine confirmed cases and one death.

The Rio city government said in an email to AFP that the patient tested positive for malaria Saturday evening and "the case remains under investigation." The Sao Paulo government said that despite the suspected case, "the technical assessment indicates that the risk of the disease being introduced into Brazil and South America remains very low." The reports from Brazil came the same day that World Health Organization chief Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus reported five patients in Africa had recovered from the Bundibugyo virus, a rare strain fueling the current outbreak. Bundibugyo has no approved treatment or vaccine. Tedros said these five cases exemplify that recovery from the illness is still possible. The WHO had said Friday that one patient recovered from the Bundibugyo virus, marking the first documented recovery of a person with a confirmed case since this outbreak began.
If confirmed, they would be the first infection cases outside Africa, since the outbreak began in DR Congo.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Health authorities in Brazil are monitoring two patients for possible Ebola infection in the country's two biggest cities, São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro.

A man, 37, from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo) "exhibited symptoms such as fever", São Paulo's state government said.

In Rio state, the health department said it had activated safety protocols after a Belgian man who arrived from Uganda showed "viral symptoms such as cough, chills and diarrhoea".

The test results for both patients should become available next week.

If confirmed, they would be the first infection cases outside Africa since the outbreak began in DR Congo.

There are now more than 1,000 suspected Ebola cases in DR Congo, with at least 246 deaths. Uganda has reported nine confirmed cases and one death.

The current outbreak has been caused by a rare strain of Ebola known as Bundibugyo, which has no proven vaccine and kills about a third of those infected.

While the two patients in Brazil are still being monitored for Ebola, they have already both been diagnosed with other conditions: in São Paulo, the man from DR Congo tested positive for meningitis, while in Rio, the Belgian patient tested positive for malaria.

Ebola viruses normally infect animals, typically fruit bats, but outbreaks among humans can sometimes start when people eat or handle infected animals.

Ebola spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person, including sweat, saliva, blood, semen, excrement, urine and vomit.

---

[Lähde: The Straits Times]
Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox

There have been more than 1,000 suspected cases of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo since an outbreak was declared on May 15, including nearly 250 deaths.

BRASILIA - Brazilian health authorities are monitoring two patients for possible Ebola infection in Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, officials said, sparking further concern of the deadly virus outbreak in central Africa spreading abroad.

A 37-year-old man from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), where the outbreak has been concentrated, “exhibited symptoms such as fever, meeting the definition of a suspected case” of Ebola, the Sao Paulo state government said in a statement on May 30.

While initial tests did not detect the Ebola virus in the patient, he is being monitored and isolated as a precautionary measure at a specialised infectious disease facility, the statement said.

The health department in Rio de Janeiro state, meanwhile, reported that it had activated safety protocols after a man from Uganda showed “viral symptoms such as cough, chills, and diarrhea.”

The Rio city government said in an email to AFP that the patient tested positive for malaria on the evening of May 30 and “the case remains under investigation.”

There have been more than 1,000 suspected cases of Ebola in the DRC since the outbreak was declared on May 15, including nearly 250 deaths, the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention said on May 28.

Several infections and one death have been confirmed in neighbouring Uganda.

However, the true reach of the outbreak in the DRC, which is thought to have been circulating before it was detected, is likely to be much wider, the World Health Organisation has warned.

The Sao Paulo government said that despite the suspected case, “the technical assessment indicates that the risk of the disease being introduced into Brazil and South America remains very low.” AFP

payload.title: Brasilia seuraa kahta mahdollista ebolatapausta São Paulossa ja Rio de Janeirossa
payload.summary: Brasilian terveysviranomaiset seuraavat kahta potilasta mahdollisen ebolatartunnan vuoksi São Paulossa ja Rio de Janeirossa. Molempien testituloksia odotetaan ensi viikolla, ja viranomaiset arvioivat taudin leviämisriskin Brasiliaan hyvin pieneksi.
payload.content:
Brasilian terveysviranomaiset seuraavat kahta potilasta mahdollisen ebolatartunnan vuoksi maan kahdessa suurimmassa kaupungissa, São Paulossa ja Rio de Janeirossa. Jos tartunnat varmistuvat, kyse olisi ensimmäisistä Afrikan ulkopuolella todetuista tapauksista sen jälkeen, kun Kongon demokraattisessa tasavallassa alkanut nykyinen epidemia käynnistyi.

## Kaksi potilasta on viranomaisten seurannassa

São Paulon osavaltio kertoi, että 37-vuotias Kongon demokraattisesta tasavallasta tullut mies oli oireillut muun muassa kuumeella. Viranomaisten mukaan oireet täyttivät epäillyn ebolatapauksen määritelmän. Tapaus mainittiin São Paulon osavaltion lausunnossa 30. toukokuuta.

Rio de Janeirossa terveysviranomaiset puolestaan aktivoivat turvallisuusprotokollat belgialaisen miehen vuoksi. Hän oli saapunut Ugandasta, ja hänellä oli virustautiin sopivia oireita, kuten yskää, vilunväristyksiä ja ripulia. Rio de Janeiron kaupunginhallinnon mukaan potilas sai lauantai-iltana positiivisen malariatestituloksen, mutta tapaus on yhä tutkinnassa.

Molempien potilaiden ebolatestien tulosten odotetaan valmistuvan ensi viikolla. São Paulon viranomaiset ovat korostaneet, että teknisen arvion mukaan taudin kulkeutumisen riski Brasiliaan ja Etelä-Amerikkaan on edelleen hyvin pieni.

## Epidemia on keskittynyt Keski-Afrikkaan

Kongon demokraattisessa tasavallassa on raportoitu yli tuhat epäiltyä ebolatapausta sen jälkeen, kun epidemia julistettiin 15. toukokuuta. Kuolemia on ilmoitettu vähintään 246, ja osa lähteistä kuvaa määrää lähes 250 kuolemaksi. Uganda on puolestaan raportoinut yhdeksän varmistettua tapausta ja yhden kuoleman.

Nykyiseen epidemiaan liittyy Bundibugyo-virus, joka on harvinainen ebolaviruksen muoto. Sille ei ole hyväksyttyä hoitoa tai rokotetta. Maailman terveysjärjestön pääjohtaja Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus kertoi, että viisi potilasta Afrikassa on toipunut Bundibugyo-viruksen aiheuttamasta taudista. WHO oli jo aiemmin kertonut yhdestä varmistetusta toipumisesta nykyisen epidemian aikana.

## Varmistusta odotetaan laboratoriotesteistä

Brasilian viranomaisten seuranta ei vielä tarkoita, että maassa olisi todettu ebolatartuntoja. Tällä hetkellä kyse on epäilyistä, joiden varmistuminen riippuu laboratoriotutkimuksista ja viranomaisten jatkoselvityksistä. Rio de Janeiron potilaan malariatulos tuo tapaukseen lisäselvitettävää, mutta viranomaiset eivät ole lähdetietojen perusteella päättäneet tutkintaa.

Mahdollisten tapausten merkitys liittyy ennen kaikkea siihen, että nykyisen epidemian vahvistetut ja epäillyt tapaukset ovat keskittyneet Afrikkaan. Siksi Brasilian testituloksia seurataan tarkasti, vaikka São Paulon viranomaisten mukaan alueellinen riski pysyy teknisen arvion perusteella hyvin matalana.

article.source_text:
Health authorities in Brazil are monitoring two patients for possible Ebola infection in the country's two biggest cities, São Paulo and Rio de Janeiro. A man, 37, from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DR Congo) "exhibited symptoms such as fever", São Paulo's state government said. In Rio state, the health department said it had activated safety protocols after a Belgian man who arrived from Uganda showed "viral symptoms such as cough, chills and diarrhoea". The test results for both patients should become available next week. If confirmed, they would be the first infection cases outside Africa since the outbreak began in DR Congo. There are now more than 1,000 suspected Ebola cases in DR Congo, with at least 246 deaths. Uganda has reported nine confirmed cases and one death.

The Rio city government said in an email to AFP that the patient tested positive for malaria Saturday evening and "the case remains under investigation." The Sao Paulo government said that despite the suspected case, "the technical assessment indicates that the risk of the disease being introduced into Brazil and South America remains very low." The reports from Brazil came the same day that World Health Organization chief Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus reported five patients in Africa had recovered from the Bundibugyo virus, a rare strain fueling the current outbreak. Bundibugyo has no approved treatment or vaccine. Tedros said these five cases exemplify that recovery from the illness is still possible. The WHO had said Friday that one patient recovered from the Bundibugyo virus, marking the first documented recovery of a person with a confirmed case since this outbreak began.

If confirmed, they would be the first infection cases outside Africa, since the outbreak began in DR Congo.

BRASILIA - Brazilian health authorities are monitoring two patients for possible Ebola infection in Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro, officials said, sparking further concern of the deadly virus outbreak in central Africa spreading abroad. A 37-year-old man from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), where the outbreak has been concentrated, “exhibited symptoms such as fever, meeting the definition of a suspected case” of Ebola, the Sao Paulo state government said in a statement on May 30.
